hints: Notice the reaction is exothermic, so think of heat as one of the products and apply Le Chatelier's principle.
Increasing temperature adds heat, so the equilibrium shifts backwards to use it up and less $\text{SO}_3$ is made.
Remember a catalyst speeds up forward and backward reactions equally, so it gets you to equilibrium faster but cannot change the final yield.
walkthrough:
**Write the Contact process equilibrium**

Think of this as a reversible, heat-releasing reaction. That detail controls everything.

Chemical equation:
$$2\text{SO}_2(g) + \text{O}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3(g) \quad \Delta H < 0$$

**Apply Le Chatelier to higher temperature**

For an exothermic reaction, heat is effectively a product. Add more heat by raising temperature and the system shifts left to oppose it.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{increase T favours endothermic direction, so yield of } \text{SO}_3 \text{ decreases}$$

**Apply the catalyst rule**

A $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ catalyst lowers the activation energy for both the forward and reverse reactions by the same amount. It makes equilibrium reached much faster, but the position of equilibrium and the equilibrium yield stay exactly the same.

Conclusion: temperature up means yield down, catalyst means yield unchanged.

options.A: The first half is right, higher temperature does lower the $\text{SO}_3$ yield. The second half is wrong because a catalyst never changes equilibrium yield, it only increases rate.
options.B: Increasing temperature shifts the exothermic equilibrium $2\text{SO}_2 + \text{O}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3$ to the left, so equilibrium yield decreases. The vanadium(V) oxide catalyst speeds up attainment of equilibrium but leaves the position and yield unchanged.
options.C: The catalyst part is correct, yield is unchanged. The temperature part is backwards, higher temperature favours the endothermic reverse reaction for an exothermic change, so yield decreases not increases.
options.D: Both parts are reversed. Higher temperature decreases yield for this exothermic reaction, and a catalyst does not increase yield at all. This row confuses faster rate with greater yield.
